title: Le Griffon, 1679: The First Ship Lost on the Upper Great Lakes

sources.what: 'was launched on 7 Aug. 1679'; 'a boat of about 45 tons'; 'he sent the Griffon back to Niagara loaded with a substantial cargo of furs'; 'according to certain Potawatomis, a storm had beyond all doubt sunk the bark'; 'stopping on 1 November at the mouth of the Riviere des Miamis (Saint-Joseph)', 'he caused a fort 40 feet by 30 to be built there'
sources.who: Dictionary of Canadian Biography, La Salle

sources.what: built 'above Niagara Falls on the shore of the Niagara River near the mouth of the Cayuga Creek'; 'On September 18, 1679, the bark Griffon was sent back'; no claimed find has sufficient evidence
sources.who: Wisconsin Shipwrecks (Wisconsin Historical Society / Sea Grant)

sources.what: 'the first vessel to sail the Upper Great Lakes other than canoes'; 'On September 18, 1679, the ship sailed east' 'with a crew of six men'; 'Neither La Salle nor Hennepin were on board'; La Salle thought his men might have stolen the furs and scuttled the ship
'First ship to sail Lakes Erie, Huron and Michigan'
'The Griffin was never heard from again'; state archaeologist Dean Anderson (2014): 'I haven't seen any evidence that suggests that anyone has found wreckage of the Griffon there'
La Salle waited at the fort at the St. Joseph River's mouth in vain for the Griffin

beats.text: The first sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes vanished on its first voyage.
beats.label: LAKE MICHIGAN, 1679
beats.credit: Brock University; Dictionary of Canadian Biography

beats.text: It was called the Griffon. The French explorer La Salle had it built in 1679, on the Niagara River above the falls.
beats.label: BUILT 1679
beats.credit: Dictionary of Canadian Biography; Wisconsin Shipwrecks

beats.text: That September it reached Green Bay, and La Salle loaded it with furs.
beats.label: GREEN BAY, SEPTEMBER 1679
beats.credit: Dictionary of Canadian Biography; Wisconsin Shipwrecks

beats.text: On September 18, he sent it back with a crew of six. La Salle stayed behind.
beats.label: SEPTEMBER 18, 1679

beats.text: The Griffon was never heard from again.
beats.label: NEVER HEARD FROM AGAIN

beats.text: That November, La Salle built a fort at the mouth of the St. Joseph River, in today's Michigan. A state marker there says he awaited his ship, and it did not come.
beats.label: ST. JOSEPH, MICHIGAN
beats.credit: Dictionary of Canadian Biography; Michigan historical marker

beats.text: A storm? A mutiny? No one knows. Wreck claims keep coming, and none has been confirmed.
beats.label: STILL MISSING

beats.text: Comment your town for the next La Porte After Dark.
